issues.failure_explanation: C^{1,1} regularity of each c_i does not give uniqueness of the Monge map or null intersections of Laguerre cells. One needs a twist-type condition, e.g. |{c_i - c_j = t}| = 0 for all i≠j and t. Counterexample allowed by the statement: two particles with equal costs (e.g. coincident centroids, which the paper explicitly permits, with the C^{1,1} L^2 cost). Then |L_i| = v_i < 1 forces w_i = w_j, so L_i = L_j = Ω. The cells overlap on full measure and any split of Ω is optimal, so the Monge map is not unique. Conversely, the C^{1,1} hypothesis excludes the power costs |x-x_i|^α with α<2 (α=0.75, 1, and α_i∈[0.5,4] in the bubbly tessellation), which the paper uses with this theorem.

issues.failure_explanation: A non-decreasing U with these limits need not attain v_i: U jumps wherever c_i has a level set of positive measure. U(0)=0 also fails if {c_i=0} has positive measure, and w* is not unique if c_i has gaps in its range. If {c_i=w} has positive measure and U(w-) < v_i < U(w), the volume-constrained minimizers are {c_i<w} plus part of {c_i=w}. These are not of the form S(w), so the lemma fails. The statement also omits the constraint |S|=v_i that the proof uses; without it the minimizer is a null set.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: which corresponds to lowering the potential and thus allowing deformations in the directions of large nonnegative gradients
This corresponds to a larger cost in the direction of larger gradient but even larger for negative gradient.

issues.failure_explanation: With phi = -log c, the perturbed cost is c = c_0 exp(-beta f). For f = -delta_+, c = c_0 exp(beta delta_+) ≥ c_0. Lowering the potential raises the cost in directions of positive gradient, so the cell shape {c ≤ w} shrinks there instead of elongating towards the attractant. Similarly, f = delta_-^2 + delta_+ ≥ 0 lowers the cost everywhere, contradicting the stated 'larger cost'. The stated mechanisms hold only for c = c_0 exp(+beta f), and the source does not fix which sign to change.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Make the sign convention consistent: either define phi = log c, or flip the signs of the perturbations in eq:perturblong and eq:perturbfan.
issues.overall_effect: As written, the cost construction for chemotactic migration (eq:perturblong, eq:perturbfan) produces shrinkage rather than protrusion towards the gradient. The claimed chemotactic behaviour does not follow from the stated definitions.
issues.title: Chemotaxis cost perturbations have the opposite effect to that claimed under phi = -log c
issues.why_classification: A local sign fix restores consistency between definition, construction and claimed behaviour, with no change to the method.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof shows only that a symmetric touching configuration is force-balanced iff cos θ = γ_ij/(2γ_0). For γ_ij ≥ 2γ_0 no θ ∈ (0, π/2) satisfies this, so the asserted equilibrium does not exist. For θ = 0 (separated disks) the same computation gives zero medium force, so separated doublets are also equilibria. The statement asserts 'the' equilibrium unconditionally.
